library(dplyr)

agency_ratio <- sr_with_sla %>%
  filter(sla_status == "measurable",
         !is.na(sla_hours),
         sla_hours > 0) %>%
  group_by(agency) %>%
  summarise(
    n_total           = n(),
    n_closed          = sum(!is.na(resolution_hours) & resolution_hours >= 0),
    pct_closed        = n_closed / n_total,
    median_resolution_hrs = median(resolution_hours[!is.na(resolution_hours) & resolution_hours >= 0]),
    median_sla_hrs    = median(sla_hours),
    ratio             = median_resolution_hrs / median_sla_hrs,
    # Compliance among CLOSED tickets only
    compliance_closed = mean(met_sla[!is.na(resolution_hours) & resolution_hours >= 0], na.rm = TRUE),
    # Compliance counting open-and-overdue as failures
    compliance_all    = mean(met_sla, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(n_total >= 100) %>%
  arrange(ratio)

print(agency_ratio, n = Inf)

flagged <- agency_ratio %>%
  filter(ratio < 0.25 | compliance_closed == 0 | compliance_closed >= 0.98 |
           compliance_all == 0)

cat("\n--- Flagged agencies ---\n")
print(flagged, n = Inf)


target_agency <- "NYPD"

agency_breakdown <- sr_with_sla %>%
  filter(sla_status == "measurable",
         agency == target_agency,
         !is.na(sla_hours),
         sla_hours > 0) %>%
  group_by(complaint_type) %>%
  summarise(
    n_total           = n(),
    n_closed          = sum(!is.na(resolution_hours) & resolution_hours >= 0),
    pct_closed        = n_closed / n_total,
    median_resolution_hrs = median(resolution_hours[!is.na(resolution_hours) & resolution_hours >= 0]),
    p25_resolution_hrs    = quantile(resolution_hours[!is.na(resolution_hours) & resolution_hours >= 0], 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    p75_resolution_hrs    = quantile(resolution_hours[!is.na(resolution_hours) & resolution_hours >= 0], 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_sla_hrs    = median(sla_hours),
    ratio             = median_resolution_hrs / median_sla_hrs,
    compliance_closed = mean(met_sla[!is.na(resolution_hours) & resolution_hours >= 0], na.rm = TRUE),
    compliance_all    = mean(met_sla, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(n_total >= 30) %>%
  arrange(ratio)

print(agency_breakdown, n = Inf)





# =============================================================================
# NYC 311 SLA Compliance Analysis — Data Pull & Join Scaffold
# Window: Jan 1, 2022 through Dec 31, 2025
#
# Datasets:
#   - 311 Service Requests from 2020 to Present  (erm2-nwe9)
#   - 311 Service Level Agreements               (cs9t-e3x8)
#
# What this script does:
#   1. Pulls the full SLA lookup table (small — ~1,500 rows).
#   2. Pulls SRs (sample mode for testing, full mode for production).
#   3. Parses the SLA "sla_days" string column into numeric hours + days.
#   4. Left-joins SLA targets onto SRs at the most granular key available.
#   5. Computes actual resolution time and SLA compliance flags.
#
# Before you run:
#   - Get a free Socrata app token: https://data.cityofnewyork.us/profile/app_tokens
#   - Set as an env var SOCRATA_APP_TOKEN, or paste into the line below.
# =============================================================================


# ---- 0. Packages -----------------------------------------------------------
pkgs <- c("RSocrata", "dplyr", "lubridate", "stringr", "tidyr", "readr", "httr", "purrr")
to_install <- pkgs[!pkgs %in% rownames(installed.packages())]
if (length(to_install)) install.packages(to_install)
invisible(lapply(pkgs, library, character.only = TRUE))

# ---- 1. Config -------------------------------------------------------------
SOCRATA_APP_TOKEN <- Sys.getenv("SOCRATA_APP_TOKEN", unset = "fY0DltbUaGfPenH6P7chzp1yf")

SR_ENDPOINT  <- "https://data.cityofnewyork.us/resource/erm2-nwe9.json"
SLA_ENDPOINT <- "https://data.cityofnewyork.us/resource/cs9t-e3x8.json"

START_DATE <- "2022-01-01T00:00:00.000"
END_DATE   <- "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000"  # exclusive upper bound = through 12/31/2025

# Switch this to FALSE when you're ready to pull the full multi-million-row SR set.
SAMPLE_ONLY <- FALSE
SAMPLE_LIMIT <- 50000

# ---- Timeout / retry tuning -------------------------------------------------
# Each Socrata page request will be given up to this many seconds before httr
# gives up. Generous ceiling — pages normally come back in < 30s but can stall
# during peak hours. You'd rather wait than crash mid-pull.
HTTP_TIMEOUT_SEC <- 600      # 10 minutes per page request
MAX_RETRIES      <- 5        # retries per chunk on transient failures (503, timeout)
RETRY_BACKOFF_SEC <- 30      # initial backoff, doubles each retry

# Chunk the full-year pull one month at a time so a failure at month 23 doesn't
# cost you months 1-22. Set FALSE if you want a single monolithic request.
CHUNK_BY_MONTH <- TRUE
CACHE_DIR      <- "socrata_cache"
dir.create(CACHE_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Anchor compliance calculations to a fixed date so re-running is reproducible.
# Tickets still open as of this date that have already exceeded their SLA
# window are treated as failures; tickets still open but within their SLA
# window are treated as not-yet-evaluable. Without this anchor, results would
# shift slightly every time the script runs.
ANALYSIS_AS_OF <- as.POSIXct("2026-01-01 00:00:00", tz = "UTC")

# Track total pipeline runtime for methodology reporting.
PIPELINE_START <- Sys.time()
message("Pipeline started: ", format(PIPELINE_START))

# Helper: run an expression with a generous HTTP timeout and retries.
safe_socrata <- function(url, token, label = url) {
  attempt <- 0
  repeat {
    attempt <- attempt + 1
    result <- tryCatch(
      httr::with_config(
        config = httr::timeout(HTTP_TIMEOUT_SEC),
        read.socrata(url, app_token = token)
      ),
      error = function(e) e
    )
    if (!inherits(result, "error")) return(result)
    if (attempt >= MAX_RETRIES) {
      stop("Failed after ", MAX_RETRIES, " attempts on ", label,
           "\nLast error: ", conditionMessage(result))
    }
    wait <- RETRY_BACKOFF_SEC * (2 ^ (attempt - 1))
    message("  Attempt ", attempt, " failed (", conditionMessage(result),
            "). Retrying in ", wait, "s...")
    Sys.sleep(wait)
  }
}

# ---- 2. Pull SLA lookup (full table, it's tiny) ----------------------------
sla_raw <- safe_socrata(SLA_ENDPOINT, SOCRATA_APP_TOKEN, "SLA lookup")
message("SLA rows pulled: ", nrow(sla_raw))

# Parse "7 days" / "1 day" / "8 hours" / "12 hours" into numeric hours.
# The column is stored as a string — this is the single most important cleaning step.
# Some rows carry the literal text "SLA Not Managed by 311" — these are real
# rows in the lookup, they just don't have a measurable target. Track them
# as their own category so they don't get silently mixed with unmatched SRs.
sla <- sla_raw %>%
  mutate(
    sla_num  = as.numeric(str_extract(sla_days, "\\d+\\.?\\d*")),
    sla_unit = str_to_lower(str_extract(sla_days, "[a-zA-Z]+")),
    sla_hours = case_when(
      sla_unit %in% c("hour", "hours") ~ sla_num,
      sla_unit %in% c("day",  "days")  ~ sla_num * 24,
      TRUE                             ~ NA_real_
    ),
    sla_days_numeric = sla_hours / 24,
    sla_status = case_when(
      !is.na(sla_hours)                                    ~ "measurable",
      str_detect(sla_days, regex("not managed", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "not_managed_by_311",
      TRUE                                                 ~ "unparseable"
    )
  ) %>%
  # Normalize the optional details columns so joins behave predictably.
  mutate(
    problem_details    = if_else(is.na(problem_details)    | problem_details    == "", "N/A", problem_details),
    additional_details = if_else(is.na(additional_details) | additional_details == "", "N/A", additional_details)
  )

# Report SLA row health — distinguish categories clearly.
cat("\n--- SLA lookup health ---\n")
sla %>% count(sla_status) %>% print()

unparseable <- sla %>% filter(sla_status == "unparseable")
if (nrow(unparseable) > 0) {
  warning("Truly unparseable sla_days values (not 'Not Managed'):\n",
          paste(unique(unparseable$sla_days), collapse = ", "))
}

# ---- 3. Pull Service Requests ---------------------------------------------
# Strategy:
#   - SAMPLE_ONLY: single small request with a server-side date filter.
#   - Full pull + CHUNK_BY_MONTH: iterate month-by-month, cache each month to
#     disk. If the session crashes, re-running picks up from the last saved
#     month rather than restarting from January 2022.
#   - Full pull + !CHUNK_BY_MONTH: one big paginated request. Simpler, more
#     fragile for long runs.

build_where <- function(start_iso, end_iso) {
  sprintf("created_date >= '%s' AND created_date < '%s'", start_iso, end_iso)
}

build_url <- function(where_clause, limit = NULL) {
  paste0(
    SR_ENDPOINT,
    "?$where=", URLencode(where_clause, reserved = TRUE),
    if (!is.null(limit)) paste0("&$limit=", limit) else ""
  )
}

if (SAMPLE_ONLY) {
  sr_url <- build_url(build_where(START_DATE, END_DATE), limit = SAMPLE_LIMIT)
  message("Pulling SR sample from:\n  ", sr_url)
  sr_raw <- safe_socrata(sr_url, SOCRATA_APP_TOKEN, "SR sample")
  
} else if (CHUNK_BY_MONTH) {
  month_starts <- seq(as.Date("2022-01-01"), as.Date("2025-12-01"), by = "1 month")
  sr_chunks <- vector("list", length(month_starts))
  
  for (i in seq_along(month_starts)) {
    m_start <- month_starts[i]
    m_end   <- seq(m_start, by = "1 month", length.out = 2)[2]
    tag     <- format(m_start, "%Y-%m")
    cache_file <- file.path(CACHE_DIR, paste0("sr_", tag, ".rds"))
    
    if (file.exists(cache_file)) {
      message("[", i, "/", length(month_starts), "] ", tag, " — cached, skipping")
      sr_chunks[[i]] <- readRDS(cache_file)
      next
    }
    
    url <- build_url(build_where(
      format(m_start, "%Y-%m-%dT00:00:00.000"),
      format(m_end,   "%Y-%m-%dT00:00:00.000")
    ))
    message("[", i, "/", length(month_starts), "] ", tag, " — pulling...")
    t0 <- Sys.time()
    chunk <- safe_socrata(url, SOCRATA_APP_TOKEN, paste("SR chunk", tag))
    message("    ", nrow(chunk), " rows in ",
            round(as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "secs")), 1), "s")
    saveRDS(chunk, cache_file)
    sr_chunks[[i]] <- chunk
  }
  sr_raw <- bind_rows(sr_chunks)
  
} else {
  sr_url <- build_url(build_where(START_DATE, END_DATE))
  message("Pulling full SR range in one shot (this may take a long time):\n  ", sr_url)
  sr_raw <- safe_socrata(sr_url, SOCRATA_APP_TOKEN, "full SR pull")
}

message("SR rows pulled: ", nrow(sr_raw))

# ---- 4. Prep SRs for join --------------------------------------------------
sr <- sr_raw %>%
  mutate(
    created_date = ymd_hms(created_date, quiet = TRUE),
    closed_date  = ymd_hms(closed_date,  quiet = TRUE),
    # Match the SLA "N/A" convention so joins work.
    descriptor   = if_else(is.na(descriptor)   | descriptor   == "", "N/A", descriptor),
    descriptor_2 = if_else(is.na(descriptor_2) | descriptor_2 == "", "N/A", descriptor_2)
  )

# ---- 5. Join SLA onto SRs --------------------------------------------------
# Strategy: try the most granular match (4 keys), fall back to 3 keys.
# Using agency_name on the SR side because SR.agency is an abbreviation and
# SLA.agency is the full name.

join4 <- sr %>%
  inner_join(
    sla %>% select(agency, problem, problem_details, additional_details,
                   sla_days, sla_hours, sla_days_numeric, sla_status),
    by = c("agency_name" = "agency",
           "complaint_type" = "problem",
           "descriptor" = "problem_details",
           "descriptor_2" = "additional_details")
  ) %>% mutate(sla_match_level = "agency+type+desc+addl")

matched_ids <- join4$unique_key

# Rows that didn't match on 4 keys — try 3.
join3 <- sr %>%
  filter(!unique_key %in% matched_ids) %>%
  inner_join(
    sla %>%
      select(agency, problem, problem_details, sla_days, sla_hours, sla_days_numeric, sla_status) %>%
      distinct(agency, problem, problem_details, .keep_all = TRUE),
    by = c("agency_name" = "agency",
           "complaint_type" = "problem",
           "descriptor" = "problem_details")
  ) %>% mutate(sla_match_level = "agency+type+desc")

matched_ids <- c(matched_ids, join3$unique_key)

# Unmatched rows — keep them but with NA SLA so you can report coverage.
unmatched <- sr %>%
  filter(!unique_key %in% matched_ids) %>%
  mutate(sla_days = NA_character_,
         sla_hours = NA_real_,
         sla_days_numeric = NA_real_,
         sla_status = "no_match",
         sla_match_level = "unmatched")

sr_with_sla <- bind_rows(join4, join3, unmatched)

# ---- 6. Compute compliance metrics ----------------------------------------
# met_sla semantics:
#   TRUE       = closed within SLA
#   FALSE      = closed past SLA, OR still open and already past SLA as of ANALYSIS_AS_OF
#   NA         = cannot be evaluated (still open and within SLA window,
#                or no matched SLA, or SLA is "not managed by 311")
sr_with_sla <- sr_with_sla %>%
  mutate(
    resolution_hours = as.numeric(difftime(closed_date, created_date, units = "hours")),
    met_sla = case_when(
      sla_status %in% c("not_managed_by_311", "no_match", "unparseable") ~ NA,
      is.na(sla_hours) ~ NA,
      is.na(closed_date) & (as.numeric(difftime(ANALYSIS_AS_OF, created_date, units = "hours")) > sla_hours) ~ FALSE,
      is.na(closed_date) ~ NA,
      resolution_hours <= sla_hours ~ TRUE,
      TRUE ~ FALSE
    )
  )

# ---- 7. Quick summaries ----------------------------------------------------
cat("\n--- SR-level SLA coverage ---\n")
sr_with_sla %>%
  count(sla_status, sla_match_level) %>%
  arrange(desc(n)) %>%
  print()

cat("\n--- SLA compliance by agency (top 15 by measurable volume) ---\n")
sr_with_sla %>%
  filter(sla_status == "measurable", !is.na(met_sla)) %>%
  group_by(agency_name) %>%
  summarise(
    n_srs   = n(),
    pct_met = mean(met_sla, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_srs)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 15) %>%
  print()

# ---- 8. Save for downstream work ------------------------------------------
saveRDS(sr_with_sla, "sr_with_sla.rds")
write_csv(sla, "sla_lookup_parsed.csv")
message("Done. Saved sr_with_sla.rds and sla_lookup_parsed.csv.")

PIPELINE_END <- Sys.time()
message("Pipeline finished: ", format(PIPELINE_END))
message("Total runtime: ", format(round(difftime(PIPELINE_END, PIPELINE_START, units = "auto"), 1)))



# =============================================================================
# NYC 311 SLA Compliance — Chunked Join (Memory-Safe)
#
# Reads each cached monthly SR file from socrata_cache/, prepares it, joins
# it against the SLA lookup, computes compliance flags, and writes the
# per-month result to processed_cache/. At the end, concatenates the small
# per-month outputs into the final sr_with_sla.rds.
#
# Why chunked: the full-data version of the prep + join holds multiple copies
# of 13.5M rows in memory simultaneously and crashes on a 16 GB Mac. Processing
# month-by-month keeps peak memory under 5 GB.
#
# Run after the data has been cached by nyc311_sla_pull.R.
# =============================================================================

# ---- 0. Packages ----
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
library(stringr)
library(tidyr)
library(readr)

# ---- 1. Config ----
CACHE_DIR_RAW       <- "socrata_cache"
CACHE_DIR_PROCESSED <- "processed_cache"
dir.create(CACHE_DIR_PROCESSED, showWarnings = FALSE)

ANALYSIS_AS_OF <- as.POSIXct("2026-01-01 00:00:00", tz = "UTC")

PIPELINE_START <- Sys.time()
message("Chunked join started: ", format(PIPELINE_START))

# ---- 2. Load and prep the SLA lookup (same as original script) ----
sla <- read_csv("sla_lookup_parsed.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(
    problem_details    = if_else(is.na(problem_details)    | problem_details    == "", "N/A", problem_details),
    additional_details = if_else(is.na(additional_details) | additional_details == "", "N/A", additional_details)
  )

message("SLA rows loaded: ", nrow(sla))

# ---- 3. Process each cached monthly file ----
raw_files <- list.files(CACHE_DIR_RAW, pattern = "^sr_\\d{4}-\\d{2}\\.rds$", full.names = TRUE)
raw_files <- sort(raw_files)
message("Found ", length(raw_files), " monthly cache files")

process_month <- function(raw_path) {
  tag <- str_extract(basename(raw_path), "\\d{4}-\\d{2}")
  out_path <- file.path(CACHE_DIR_PROCESSED, paste0("sr_with_sla_", tag, ".rds"))
  
  if (file.exists(out_path)) {
    message("[", tag, "] processed file exists — skipping")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  
  t0 <- Sys.time()
  message("[", tag, "] reading raw...")
  sr_raw <- readRDS(raw_path)
  
  # Prep
  sr <- sr_raw %>%
    mutate(
      created_date = ymd_hms(created_date, quiet = TRUE),
      closed_date  = ymd_hms(closed_date,  quiet = TRUE),
      descriptor   = if_else(is.na(descriptor)   | descriptor   == "", "N/A", descriptor),
      descriptor_2 = if_else(is.na(descriptor_2) | descriptor_2 == "", "N/A", descriptor_2)
    )
  rm(sr_raw); gc(verbose = FALSE)
  
  # 4-key join
  join4 <- sr %>%
    inner_join(
      sla %>% select(agency, problem, problem_details, additional_details,
                     sla_days, sla_hours, sla_days_numeric, sla_status),
      by = c("agency_name" = "agency",
             "complaint_type" = "problem",
             "descriptor" = "problem_details",
             "descriptor_2" = "additional_details")
    ) %>% mutate(sla_match_level = "agency+type+desc+addl")
  
  matched_ids <- join4$unique_key
  
  # 3-key fallback
  join3 <- sr %>%
    filter(!unique_key %in% matched_ids) %>%
    inner_join(
      sla %>%
        select(agency, problem, problem_details, sla_days, sla_hours, sla_days_numeric, sla_status) %>%
        distinct(agency, problem, problem_details, .keep_all = TRUE),
      by = c("agency_name" = "agency",
             "complaint_type" = "problem",
             "descriptor" = "problem_details")
    ) %>% mutate(sla_match_level = "agency+type+desc")
  
  matched_ids <- c(matched_ids, join3$unique_key)
  
  # Unmatched
  unmatched <- sr %>%
    filter(!unique_key %in% matched_ids) %>%
    mutate(sla_days = NA_character_,
           sla_hours = NA_real_,
           sla_days_numeric = NA_real_,
           sla_status = "no_match",
           sla_match_level = "unmatched")
  
  rm(sr); gc(verbose = FALSE)
  
  sr_with_sla_month <- bind_rows(join4, join3, unmatched)
  rm(join4, join3, unmatched); gc(verbose = FALSE)
  
  # Compliance metrics
  sr_with_sla_month <- sr_with_sla_month %>%
    mutate(
      resolution_hours = as.numeric(difftime(closed_date, created_date, units = "hours")),
      met_sla = case_when(
        sla_status %in% c("not_managed_by_311", "no_match", "unparseable") ~ NA,
        is.na(sla_hours) ~ NA,
        is.na(closed_date) & (as.numeric(difftime(ANALYSIS_AS_OF, created_date, units = "hours")) > sla_hours) ~ FALSE,
        is.na(closed_date) ~ NA,
        resolution_hours <= sla_hours ~ TRUE,
        TRUE ~ FALSE
      )
    )
  
  saveRDS(sr_with_sla_month, out_path)
  elapsed <- round(as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "secs")), 1)
  message("[", tag, "] processed ", nrow(sr_with_sla_month), " rows in ", elapsed, "s")
  
  rm(sr_with_sla_month); gc(verbose = FALSE)
  invisible(NULL)
}

for (f in raw_files) {
  process_month(f)
}

# ---- 4. Concatenate per-month outputs ----
message("Concatenating processed monthly files...")
processed_files <- list.files(CACHE_DIR_PROCESSED, pattern = "^sr_with_sla_\\d{4}-\\d{2}\\.rds$", full.names = TRUE)
processed_files <- sort(processed_files)

# Use a list and bind_rows once at the end. This is the only step that needs
# all data in memory simultaneously, but no intermediate copies are made.
sr_with_sla_list <- lapply(processed_files, readRDS)
sr_with_sla <- bind_rows(sr_with_sla_list)
rm(sr_with_sla_list); gc(verbose = FALSE)

message("Final row count: ", nrow(sr_with_sla))

# ---- 5. Quick summaries ----
cat("\n--- SR-level SLA coverage ---\n")
sr_with_sla %>%
  count(sla_status, sla_match_level) %>%
  arrange(desc(n)) %>%
  print()

cat("\n--- SLA compliance by agency (top 15 by measurable volume) ---\n")
sr_with_sla %>%
  filter(sla_status == "measurable", !is.na(met_sla)) %>%
  group_by(agency_name) %>%
  summarise(
    n_srs   = n(),
    pct_met = mean(met_sla, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_srs)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 15) %>%
  print()

# ---- 6. Save final output ----
saveRDS(sr_with_sla, "sr_with_sla.rds")
message("Done. Saved sr_with_sla.rds")

PIPELINE_END <- Sys.time()
message("Chunked join finished: ", format(PIPELINE_END))
message("Total runtime: ", format(round(difftime(PIPELINE_END, PIPELINE_START, units = "auto"), 1)))





Final visual:

# =============================================================================
# NYC 311 SLA Compliance — Visualization 1 (alternative): Diverging Bar
#
# Each agency's bar shows log2(actual median resolution / SLA target).
# Bars to the left of center (0) = beating SLA; bars to the right = missing SLA.
# Y-axis labels include both the absolute SLA and compliance %.
#
# Saves to a different filename so the lollipop version stays as a backup.
# =============================================================================

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
library(stringr)
library(readr)

if (!exists("sr_with_sla")) {
  sr_with_sla <- readRDS("sr_with_sla.rds")
}

dir.create("figures", showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create("tables",  showWarnings = FALSE)

# ---- Compute summary ----
agency_summary <- sr_with_sla %>%
  filter(sla_status == "measurable",
         !is.na(sla_hours), sla_hours > 0) %>%
  group_by(agency_name) %>%
  summarise(
    n_total = n(),
    n_closed = sum(!is.na(resolution_hours) & resolution_hours >= 0),
    median_resolution_hrs = median(resolution_hours[!is.na(resolution_hours) & resolution_hours >= 0]),
    median_sla_hrs = median(sla_hours),
    ratio = median_resolution_hrs / median_sla_hrs,
    log2_ratio = log2(ratio),
    compliance_all = mean(met_sla, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(n_total >= 1000) %>%
  arrange(ratio)

# Format the absolute SLA target into something readable.
# 8 hours stays "8 hr"; 24 hours becomes "1 day"; 168 becomes "1 wk", etc.
format_sla <- function(hrs) {
  case_when(
    hrs < 24                ~ paste0(round(hrs), " hr"),
    hrs < 24 * 7            ~ paste0(round(hrs / 24), " day"),
    hrs < 24 * 30           ~ paste0(round(hrs / (24 * 7)), " wk"),
    hrs < 24 * 365          ~ paste0(round(hrs / (24 * 30)), " mo"),
    TRUE                    ~ paste0(round(hrs / (24 * 365), 1), " yr")
  )
}

agency_summary <- agency_summary %>%
  mutate(
    short_name = case_when(
      agency_name == "New York City Police Department"                    ~ "NYPD",
      agency_name == "Department of Sanitation"                            ~ "DSNY",
      agency_name == "Department of Parks and Recreation"                  ~ "DPR",
      agency_name == "Department of Transportation"                        ~ "DOT",
      agency_name == "Department of Health and Mental Hygiene"             ~ "DOHMH",
      agency_name == "Economic Development Corporation"                    ~ "EDC",
      agency_name == "Taxi and Limousine Commission"                       ~ "TLC",
      agency_name == "Department of Consumer and Worker Protection"        ~ "DCWP",
      agency_name == "Department of Homeless Services"                     ~ "DHS",
      agency_name == "Department of Housing Preservation and Development"  ~ "HPD",
      agency_name == "Department of Education"                             ~ "DOE",
      agency_name == "Department of Environmental Protection"              ~ "DEP",
      TRUE ~ agency_name
    ),
    classification = case_when(
      short_name %in% c("NYPD", "DOHMH", "EDC", "HPD")    ~ "Measurement issues",
      compliance_all >= 0.60                              ~ "Meets SLA reliably",
      TRUE                                                ~ "Systematically misses"
    ),
    sla_label = format_sla(median_sla_hrs),
    y_label = sprintf("%s  (%s SLA, %.0f%% compliant)",
                      short_name, sla_label, compliance_all * 100),
    y_label = factor(y_label, levels = rev(y_label))
  )

write_csv(agency_summary, "tables/tbl1_agency_summary.csv")

# ---- Build figure ----
group_colors <- c(
  "Meets SLA reliably"     = "#1f4e79",
  "Systematically misses"  = "#c0392b",
  "Measurement issues"     = "#7f7f7f"
)

# log2 ratio breaks: each unit on the x-axis = doubling/halving of ratio.
x_breaks <- c(-3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3)
x_labels <- c("8x faster\nthan SLA", "4x faster", "2x faster",
              "Matches\nSLA",
              "2x slower", "4x slower", "8x slower\nthan SLA")

p1 <- ggplot(agency_summary, aes(y = y_label, x = log2_ratio,
                                 fill = classification)) +
  # Reference lines for ½×, 2×, 4× to give visual scale anchors
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-2, -1, 1, 2), color = "#eeeeee", linewidth = 0.5) +
  # The bar itself
  geom_col(width = 0.7, alpha = 0.92) +
  # Center line (matches SLA)
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "#222222", linewidth = 0.6) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = x_breaks,
    labels = x_labels,
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.05))
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = group_colors, name = NULL) +
  guides(
    fill = guide_legend(
      override.aes = list(alpha = 0.92)
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Agency Resolution Times Compared to SLA Commitments",
    subtitle = "Each bar shows the gap between actual median resolution time and the published SLA, on a doubling scale.",
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL,
    caption = paste0(
      "Jan 2022 - Dec 2025; n = ",
      format(sum(agency_summary$n_total), big.mark = ","),
      " service requests with measurable SLA. ",
      "Source: NYC OpenData (erm2-nwe9, cs9t-e3x8)."
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14,
                              margin = margin(b = 4)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "#444444", size = 10,
                                 margin = margin(b = 14)),
    plot.caption = element_text(color = "#777777", size = 8,
                                hjust = 0,
                                margin = margin(t = 12)),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.justification = "left",
    legend.margin = margin(b = 10),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 1),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9, color = "#555555",
                               lineheight = 0.85),
    plot.margin = margin(14, 14, 14, 14)
  )

ggsave("figures/fig1_agency_diverging_bars.png", p1,
       width = 11, height = 6, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
ggsave("figures/fig1_agency_diverging_bars.pdf", p1,
       width = 11, height = 6)

message("Saved figures/fig1_agency_diverging_bars.{png,pdf}")
print(p1)
